content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], Thanks for your input. I'm trying to achieve a similar setup. My main challenge is connecting the GSM unit to the [product_name]. Since the GSM modem provides only a 2.8V output, how do you convert this to work with the 24V or 12V DC inputs required by the [product_name] so it registers correctly? Do you have suggestions for converting pulses from the [product_name] relay or transistor outputs (from 12V / 24V DC down to 2.8V) back to the modem? Thanks for any ideas! Thread split from: Select which relay to switch based on number of pulses on a single input.
Hello [user_name], I'm not sure of your electronics background, but using optocouplers would accomplish what you need. [url] Hope this helps.
Hi, If you have analog inputs available, you can also use them to detect a 2.8V signal. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, I've now managed to get everything working as intended. I pulse the output from the GSM unit (which is low voltage) to trigger a 12V relay, which then switches 220V on a single input of the [product_name]. The [product_name] counts the pulses at the input and switches an output depending on the pulse count. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are discussing how to interface a GSM modem with a [product_name] controller, focusing on adapting voltage levels between the modem's low voltage output and the controller's higher voltage input requirements. Suggestions include using optocouplers or analog inputs for voltage conversion and pulse detection. There is also discussion about enabling bidirectional pulse signaling. The primary challenge is hardware interfacing and the lack of straightforward guidance for integrating devices with different voltage levels.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want an easily applicable solution to connect low-voltage outputs from the GSM modem to the [product_name] controller, and a simple way to allow [product_name] outputs to trigger actions on the GSM modem.
